current_activity: Walcheren: 157th Brigade relieves the Canadians at the causeway and wades the Sloe Channel at 03:30 on 3 Nov
notes: Event date: 3 November 1944, 03:30 (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 111, 114). Event definition: After the Canadian attacks of 31 October and 1-2 November, a battalion of the 157th Brigade relieves the Canadians at the Walcheren causeway on 2 November under cover of Typhoon rockets; at 03:30 on the 3rd the brigade outflanks the causeway by crossing the Sloe Channel in boats and wading a mile along the mud shore, without serious opposition; the 156th Brigade follows on the 4th and both brigades then link up and advance towards Middelburg (p. 114); the earlier landing on South Beveland, with the leading troops of the division crossing the Scheldt, is dated about 26 October (p. 111). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 114: "Then under cover of a heavy rocket attack by Typhoons they were relieved by a battalion of the 157th Brigade of the 52nd (Lowland) Division"; "At 3.30 on the morning of the 3rd this was done without serious opposition"; p. 111: "the 52nd Division's leading troops had crossed the Scheldt and were landing on South Beveland". Location: Sloedam (Walcheren causeway), Zeeland (existing place PL0685) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the Sloedam causeway, where the brigade crossed the channel; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names the Walcheren causeway and the Sloe Channel crossing (p. 114). Review (British Batch 2, 28 October 2026; inferred value; old value: operation_id OP-SCHELDT; new value: operation_id OP-INFATUATE): the row describes the fighting on Walcheren on 2 to 6 November 1944, the assault that Stacey, pp. 379-380 and 407, names Operation Infatuate (Infatuate I at Flushing, Infatuate II at Westkapelle; Ellis, vol. II, p. 114, dates the attack to 1 November and p. 123 the end to 8 November); the new operation is a child of OP-SCHELDT, so the narrower operation replaces the broader one. The Canadian Army row of 8 November (C1283) stays under OP-SCHELDT because it also closes the whole Scheldt battle.

current_activity: Blackcock: attacks along the Sittard-Heinsberg axis at dawn; a three-mile bridgehead and Hongen by dark
notes: Event date: 18 January 1945, dawn (Ellis, vol. II, p. 244). Event definition: The division begins its attack on the Sittard-Heinsberg axis at dawn on 18 January, after concentrations from most of the artillery in XII Corps, with the 156th Brigade in the lead and mine-clearing, flame-throwing and bridging tanks of the 79th Armoured Division; the ground is mud and it is two hours before the first assault bridge is launched, but a three-mile-wide bridgehead is gained and by dark Hongen, an outpost guarding the road, has been captured; the second brigade (the 157th) crosses next morning (p. 244). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 244: "The 52nd Division had begun its attack on the Sittard—Heinsberg axis at dawn on the 18th"; "by which time Hongen had been captured". Location: Hongen, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is Hongen, the outpost captured on the first day; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Hongen as the outpost captured on the first day (p. 244).

current_activity: Blackcock: 155th Brigade enters Waldfeucht early; after fierce fighting the town is cleared by midnight
notes: Event date: the early hours of 21 January 1945 to midnight (Ellis, vol. II, pp. 244, 245). Event definition: In the early hours of 21 January the 155th Brigade enters Waldfeucht from the west; after daylight the town is heavily shelled and struck by a counter-attack with Tiger tanks that produces some of the fiercest fighting of the XII Corps operation; the Scottish infantry destroy both Tigers with 6-pdr anti-tank guns, the Germans begin to retreat before dark and by midnight all are completely ejected from Waldfeucht (pp. 244-245). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. II, p. 244: "in the early hours of the 21st the 155th Brigade entered Wald- feucht from the west"; p. 245: "by midnight all were completely ejected from Waldfeucht". Location: Waldfeucht, North Rhine-Westphalia (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is the town centre of Waldfeucht; the division headquarters is not named. Location support: Ellis names Waldfeucht as the town entered and cleared (pp. 244-245).
